class.name: TireData
class.brief_description: Tire grip, transient slip response, and aligning feedback in readable units.
class.description: TireData configures the tire model using grip coefficients, response times in milliseconds, and aligning lever settings. Numeric settings are copied to each [Wheel] during vehicle setup; apply edits with [method Vehicle.restart]. Advanced properties use an ordinary collapsible Inspector group. The default lateral response uses tanh and has no force peak. Custom curves replace that response shape.

members.member: Longitudinal grip coefficient at the setup reference wheel load. Higher values increase acceleration and braking force.
Lateral grip coefficient at the setup reference wheel load. Higher values increase cornering force.

Longitudinal slip ratio corresponding to X=1 on [member forward_friction_curve]. A value of 0.15 means 15% slip; place the curve peak at X=1. Slip ratio is wheel tread speed minus contact forward speed, divided by sqrt(forward_speed squared + 9). This smooth 3 m/s regularization avoids singular slip near rest. Lower values build longitudinal force sooner. Without a custom curve, this is the scale where tanh reaches about 76% of its force limit. ABS uses this ratio as its release threshold. Range 0.01-1.

Slip angle in degrees at which the default tanh response reaches about 76% of its force limit. Lower values build cornering force sooner. This also sets the angle where pneumatic aligning trail has fully faded. Custom curves use it as their normalized-angle scale.

Grip coefficient reduction at twice the setup reference wheel load, in percent. Default approximately 6.7%; zero disables load sensitivity. At 10%, doubling load gives 90% of the coefficient and 1.8 times total force capacity. The reference load is calculated from equal mass per axle and wheel. Range 0-18.77476% corresponds to exponents 0-0.3; the runtime multiplier remains clamped to 0.75-1.25.
Tread width in metres, used for skid-mark width.
Maximum brake torque at full brake input, in Nm.

Slip-state response time constant at zero contact forward speed, in milliseconds. Slip velocity and angle reach about 63% of a constant target after this time and 90% after 2.303 times this time. Zero uses instantaneous slip. The existing property name is retained; forces are generated from relaxed slip and limited using current load and grip. Both slip directions share this time constant.

Slip-state response time constant at and above 108 km/h contact forward speed, in milliseconds. Interpolated linearly using absolute longitudinal contact-point speed. Zero uses instantaneous slip. The exponential update preserves response to a constant target across physics rates and tire substeps.

Effective aligning lever before slip-dependent rolloff, in millimetres. Higher values increase self-aligning torque. A 40 mm lever produces 40 Nm per 1000 N of lateral force before rolloff and rack scaling. This is a simplified effective lever, not a caster-geometry calculation.

Percentage of the aligning lever retained at and beyond [member lateral_response_angle]. Lower values make aligning feedback fade more during a slide. This is a lever ratio, not the fraction of actual torque retained, since lateral force also changes. Mechanical trail equals total times this fraction; pneumatic trail is the remainder.
Advanced rotational bearing-drag coefficient. Higher values slow wheel spin faster.
Advanced normalized-force superellipse exponent, clamped to 1-16. Two gives a friction ellipse. Higher values permit more simultaneous cornering and acceleration/braking force.

Optional longitudinal force curve, editable in the Inspector's Grip Curves group. X is absolute relaxed slip velocity divided by the regularized contact speed and [member peak_slip_ratio], clamped to 0-2. Y is force as a fraction of current longitudinal grip capacity. Use a 0-2 domain, start at (0,0), peak at (1,1), then fall gradually toward sliding grip at X=2. Overrides the default tanh shape.

Optional lateral force curve, editable in the Inspector's Grip Curves group. X is absolute relaxed slip angle divided by [member lateral_response_angle], clamped to 0-2. Y is force as a fraction of current lateral grip capacity. Use a 0-2 domain, start at (0,0) with a nonzero right tangent, peak at (1,1), then fall gradually toward sliding grip at X=2. Overrides the default tanh shape.
